title: Repository skeleton: web app, Postgres schema and migrations, deployment-profile loader, CI (typecheck, unit tests)
acceptance: a clean clone builds and typechecks with one command and CI runs it on every pull request

every operator-facing value (product name, upstream URL, tool visibility, credential fields, plans, feature flags) is read from profiles/*.json validated by a JSON schema in the repository; no product or customer word is hard-coded
the app starts against an empty Postgres database and migrations create every table
note: Generalisation phase: after the product is pinned as-is and re-minted (operator decision 2026-10-20), extract this capability into the general shell. Sign-in: built-in emailed code + Google, Clerk optional.

title: Fake upstream MCP server for tests (Streamable HTTP and legacy HTTP+SSE)
acceptance: it serves both protocol generations, plus a legacy HTTP+SSE mode: the stateless 2026-07-28 revision (server/discover, _meta, Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name headers, subscriptions/listen) and a session-based 2025-11-25 mode (initialize, Mcp-Session-Id, GET stream)

a stand-alone test server with: a no-credential tool, a tool that needs a per-user API key header, a tool that needs a third-party OAuth token, a slow tool, a tool that errors, a resource and a prompt
it can change its tool list at runtime and announces the change (on subscriptions/listen in 2026-07-28 mode, with notifications/tools/list_changed in the older modes)
it echoes the credential it received in a test-only field so a test can prove which user's secret was forwarded
it runs locally and in CI with one command
note: Generalisation phase: after the product is pinned as-is and re-minted (operator decision 2026-10-20), extract this capability into the general shell. Sign-in: built-in emailed code + Google, Clerk optional.

title: Users, workspaces, memberships and invites, isolated per workspace at the database
acceptance: every workspace-owned table carries workspace_id and is protected by row-level security that fails closed when no workspace is set, under a non-owner database role
a test as a member of workspace A reads and writes nothing of workspace B through any route
roles: owner, admin, member; invites by email expire and are single use
note: Generalisation phase: after the product is pinned as-is and re-minted (operator decision 2026-10-20), extract this capability into the general shell. Sign-in: built-in emailed code + Google, Clerk optional.

acceptance: a new person signs up and signs in with an emailed code; Google sign-in works when its client id is set and is hidden when it is not
sessions are httpOnly, expire, and are revoked by sign-out-everywhere
sign-in attempts are rate limited per address and per IP

title: Upstream introspection: server/discover (or initialize), tools/list, resources/list, prompts/list, stored as versioned snapshots
acceptance: given only the upstream URL (and an operator credential if it needs one), the app detects which protocol revision the upstream speaks and records its server info, its capabilities and every tool, resource and prompt, following pagination cursors
each snapshot is hashed; a new snapshot is stored only when something changed
introspection runs on deploy, on a schedule and when the upstream announces a changed tool list; a failure is recorded, not thrown
note: Generalisation phase: after the product is pinned as-is and re-minted (operator decision 2026-10-20), extract this capability into the general shell. Sign-in: built-in emailed code + Google, Clerk optional.

title: Metering gateway: an MCP endpoint per app that authenticates the caller, filters tools, forwards to the upstream and streams the answer back
acceptance: one Streamable HTTP endpoint serves 2026-07-28 clients (stateless; Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name and MCP-Protocol-Version headers validated against the body; Mcp-Param-* headers forwarded; subscriptions/listen) and 2025-11-25-and-older clients (initialize, sessions, GET stream). It forwards to an upstream of either generation or to legacy HTTP+SSE, streaming responses through
Origin is validated; the tool list a caller sees depends only on the caller's authorization, never on connection state
tools the profile hides are absent from tools/list and refused on tools/call
the caller's token for the gateway is never forwarded upstream; only the upstream credential the profile declares is sent
upstream timeouts, size caps and errors become well-formed MCP errors; the gateway never hangs a client
measured against the fake upstream: added latency per call recorded in the CI report
note: Generalisation phase: after the product is pinned as-is and re-minted (operator decision 2026-10-20), extract this capability into the general shell. Sign-in: built-in emailed code + Google, Clerk optional.

acceptance: a signed-in user creates, names, lists and revokes tokens scoped to one workspace; only a hash is stored and the value is shown once
a revoked or expired token is refused on the next call
a token of workspace A cannot reach workspace B's credentials, usage or tools
note: Generalisation phase: after the product is pinned as-is and re-minted (operator decision 2026-10-20), extract this capability into the general shell. Sign-in: built-in emailed code + Google, Clerk optional.

dashboards: calls per tool, errors, p50/p95 latency, daily and weekly active users, and week-over-week retention, for a workspace (its members) and for the operator (all workspaces)
recording never blocks or fails the call it describes
note: Generalisation phase: after the product is pinned as-is and re-minted (operator decision 2026-10-20), extract this capability into the general shell. Sign-in: built-in emailed code + Google, Clerk optional.

title: Credential vault: per-user and per-workspace secrets the upstream needs, encrypted, injected on forward
acceptance: credential fields come from the profile (name, label, help, where it is injected: header, query or bearer; per user or per workspace)

values are encrypted at rest with an envelope key from the deployment's environment, with a key id so the key can rotate; they are never logged, never returned to the browser after saving, and never put in usage records
a test with two users on the fake upstream proves each call carries its own caller's secret and never the other's, including under concurrent calls
a call to a tool whose credential is missing returns a clear MCP error naming the setup page, or a URL-mode elicitation when the client declares support for it
note: Generalisation phase: after the product is pinned as-is and re-minted (operator decision 2026-10-20), extract this capability into the general shell. Sign-in: built-in emailed code + Google, Clerk optional.

title: MCP OAuth 2.1 for clients: protected resource metadata, authorization server, client registration, PKCE, audience-bound tokens
acceptance: the gateway answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header naming its protected resource metadata (RFC 9728, at both the path-inserted and the root well-known URI). Authorization server metadata is served by RFC 8414 and by OIDC discovery with an exact issuer, and the authorization response returns iss

clients register by Client ID Metadata Document (advertised with client_id_metadata_document_supported, fetched with SSRF guards), with dynamic client registration only as a deprecated fallback. PKCE S256 is required and advertised. The resource parameter is required, and the token's audience is the gateway's own MCP address. A call with insufficient scope gets 403 so the client can step up
access tokens are short-lived and workspace-scoped, refresh tokens rotate, and the consent screen names the client and the workspace
Claude (connectors), ChatGPT and VS Code complete the sign-in against a deployment
note: Generalisation phase: after the product is pinned as-is and re-minted (operator decision 2026-10-20), extract this capability into the general shell. Sign-in: built-in emailed code + Google, Clerk optional.

the OAuth state is bound to the user and workspace and checked on return
